Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: What is the value of (25² − 15²) ÷ 40?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.explanation_en: The expression is a² + b² + 2ab with a = 0.8, b = 0.2, which equals (a + b)² = (1.0)² = 1. Directly: 0.64 + 0.04 + 0.32 = 1.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: Simplify: 7/8 of 96 − 5/6 of 72
questions.explanation_en: 7/8 of 96 = 84 and 5/6 of 72 = 60. The difference is 84 − 60 = 24.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: Find the value of 48.5% of 1200 + 12.5% of 640.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: If the 6-digit number 52x34y is divisible by 72, what is the maximum possible value of (x + y)?
questions.explanation_en: 72 = 8 × 9. For 8, the last three digits 34y must be divisible by 8: only 344 works, so y = 4. For 9, the digit sum 5 + 2 + x + 3 + 4 + 4 = 18 + x must be a multiple of 9, so x = 0 or 9. Maximum x + y = 9 + 4 = 13.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: When 1352, 2169 and 3158 are divided by the greatest possible number n, the remainder is r in each case. What is the value of (n + r)?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: Let N be the least number which, when divided by 12, 15, 20 and 54, leaves a remainder of 8 in each case, and N is divisible by 11. What is the sum of the digits of N?
questions.explanation_en: LCM(12, 15, 20, 54) = 2² × 3³ × 5 = 540, so N = 540k + 8. Since 540 = 11 × 49 + 1, N leaves remainder k + 8 on division by 11; k = 3 makes it 11. N = 540 × 3 + 8 = 1628 = 11 × 148. Digit sum = 1 + 6 + 2 + 8 = 17.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: The value of 3/4 of 2 2/3 ÷ 1 1/3 of 3/8 + 1/2 is:
questions.explanation_en: 'of' is done before ÷. 3/4 of 8/3 = 2, and 4/3 of 3/8 = 1/2. Then 2 ÷ 1/2 = 4, and 4 + 1/2 = 4 1/2. Doing ÷ before 'of' gives the wrong 1 1/16.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: The decimal 0.47̄ (only the 7 recurring) written as a fraction is:
questions.explanation_en: Mixed recurring rule: (all the digits − the non-recurring part) ÷ (one 9 for each recurring digit followed by one 0 for each non-recurring digit) = (47 − 4)/90 = 43/90. 47/99 would be 0.4747… (both digits recurring).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: How many factors (divisors) does 540 have?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: What is the unit digit of 3^65 × 6^59 × 7^71?
questions.explanation_en: Unit digits of 3 cycle 3, 9, 7, 1: 65 = 4 × 16 + 1 → 3. Any power of 6 ends in 6. Unit digits of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1: 71 = 4 × 17 + 3 → 3. Product of unit digits 3 × 6 × 3 = 54 → unit digit 4.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: What is the value of 48 ÷ 12 × 3 + 64 ÷ 8 × 2 − 15 ÷ 5 × 4?
questions.explanation_en: Division and multiplication from left to right first: 48 ÷ 12 × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12; 64 ÷ 8 × 2 = 8 × 2 = 16; 15 ÷ 5 × 4 = 3 × 4 = 12. Then 12 + 16 − 12 = 16.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Number System, LCM–HCF & Simplification
questions.question_en: What is the sum of all two-digit numbers that are divisible by 6?
questions.explanation_en: Two-digit multiples of 6 run from 12 to 96: count = (96 − 12)/6 + 1 = 15. Sum = n/2 × (first + last) = 15/2 × (12 + 96) = 15 × 54 = 810.
questions.subtopic: Number system – sum of an arithmetic sequence

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
questions.explanation_en: Let the number be 100. After +20% → 120. After −20% of 120 (= 24) → 96. Net = 4% decrease. (Rule: x − y − xy/100 = 20 − 20 − 4 = −4.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The population of a town is 25,000. If it increases by 10% every year, what will it be after 2 years?
questions.explanation_en: Population = 25000 × (1.1)² = 25000 × 1.21 = 30,250. (30,000 is what simple growth would give; 27,500 is only one year's growth.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: In an examination, the pass mark is 40%. A student scores 120 marks and fails by 20 marks. What are the maximum marks?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The price of sugar increases by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its expenditure remains unchanged?
questions.explanation_en: Reduction % = r / (100 + r) × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%. (Taking 25% is the common mistake.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: If x is 20% more than y, then y is what percent less than x?
questions.explanation_en: Let y = 100, so x = 120. y is less than x by 20, i.e. 20/120 × 100 = 16 2/3%.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: Ravi spends 80% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 10%, what is the percentage increase in his savings?
questions.explanation_en: Take income = 100: expenditure 80, saving 20. New income 120, new expenditure 88, new saving 32. Increase = 12/20 × 100 = 60%.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then A : B : C is:
questions.explanation_en: Make B equal: multiply the first ratio by 4 and the second by 3. A : B = 8 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 15, so A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.
questions.subtopic: Ratio – compound ratio A : B : C

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 10 is added to each, the ratio becomes 5 : 7. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanation_en: Let the numbers be 3x and 5x. (3x + 10)/(5x + 10) = 5/7 gives 21x + 70 = 25x + 50, so x = 5. Smaller number = 15 (the numbers are 15 and 25).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: ₹810 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/6. What is A's share?
questions.explanation_en: Multiply by 6: 3 : 2 : 1 (sum 6). A's share = 3/6 × 810 = ₹405.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 2. If each saves ₹1,600, what is A's income?
questions.explanation_en: Let incomes be 5x, 4x and expenses 3y, 2y. 5x − 3y = 1600 and 4x − 2y = 1600. From the second, y = 2x − 800. Substituting: 5x − 6x + 2400 = 1600, so x = 800. A's income = 5 × 800 = ₹4,000 (B's income is ₹3,200).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The average age of 40 students is 15 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises to 16 years. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation_en: Total with teacher = 41 × 16 = 656. Total of students = 40 × 15 = 600. Teacher's age = 656 − 600 = 56 years.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?
questions.explanation_en: Sum of first six + sum of last six = 6 × 49 + 6 × 52 = 294 + 312 = 606. This counts the sixth result twice. Total of all 11 = 550, so sixth result = 606 − 550 = 56.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A batsman scores 61 runs in his 12th innings and thereby raises his average by 3. What is his average after the 12th innings?
questions.explanation_en: Let the average after 11 innings be x. 11x + 61 = 12(x + 3) gives x = 25. New average = 28.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation_en: Total weight increases by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg. New person's weight = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A trader sells an article at a loss of 20% for ₹640. What is its cost price?
questions.subtopic: Profit & loss – cost price from loss

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: What single discount is equivalent to successive discounts of 20% and 10%?
questions.explanation_en: Net multiplier = 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so the net discount = 28%. (Adding to 30% is the common mistake.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A shopkeeper marks his goods 25% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation_en: Let CP = 100. Marked price = 125. SP = 125 × 0.9 = 112.5. Profit = 12.5%.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: Two articles are sold at ₹1,200 each, one at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss of 20%. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation_en: CP of first = 1200/1.2 = 1000; CP of second = 1200/0.8 = 1500. Total CP = 2500, total SP = 2400. Loss = 100, i.e. 4% of 2500 (formula: loss % = (20/10)² = 4%).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The cost price of 12 articles is equal to the selling price of 10 articles. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation_en: 12 CP = 10 SP, so SP/CP = 12/10 = 1.2. Profit = 20%.
questions.subtopic: Profit & loss – articles bought and sold

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A man sells an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for ₹150 more, he would have gained 5%. What is the cost price?
questions.explanation_en: The difference between 105% and 90% of CP is 15% of CP = ₹150. So CP = 150/0.15 = ₹1,000.
questions.subtopic: Profit & loss – change in selling price

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A sum of money amounts to ₹6,600 in 5 years at 10% per annum simple interest. What is the sum?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: What is the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on ₹5,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years?
questions.explanation_en: For 2 years the difference = P(R/100)² = 5000 × (0.1)² = ₹50. (CI = 1050, SI = 1000.)
questions.subtopic: CI and SI – difference for 2 years

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: At what rate of simple interest per annum will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
questions.explanation_en: Interest = P in 8 years, so P = P × R × 8 / 100, giving R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A sum of money invested at 8% compound interest per annum amounts to ₹5,832 in 2 years. What is the sum?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: What is the compound interest on ₹12,000 for 1.5 years at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.explanation_en: Rate per half-year = 5%, number of half-years = 3. Amount = 12000 × 1.05³ = 12000 × 1.157625 = 13,891.50. CI = ₹1,891.50. (₹1,800 is the simple interest.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The simple interest on a sum of money for 2 years at 5% per annum is ₹500. What is the compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for 2 years?
questions.subtopic: CI and SI – from SI to CI

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A father is 3 times as old as his son. After 12 years he will be twice as old as his son. What is the present age of the son?
questions.explanation_en: Let the son be S, father 3S. 3S + 12 = 2(S + 12), so S = 12 (father is 36).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 6 years the ratio will be 3 : 4. What is the present age of A?
questions.explanation_en: Let the ages be 5x and 7x. (5x + 6)/(7x + 6) = 3/4 gives 20x + 24 = 21x + 18, so x = 6. A = 30 years (B = 42 years).
questions.subtopic: Problems on ages – ratio of ages

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: The sum of the ages of a mother and her daughter is 56 years. Four years ago the mother's age was 7 times the daughter's age. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation_en: Let the daughter be D, mother M = 56 − D. M − 4 = 7(D − 4) gives 52 − D = 7D − 28, so D = 10 and M = 46. Check: 42 = 7 × 6.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: Six years ago the ratio of the ages of A and B was 6 : 5. Four years from now it will be 11 : 10. What is the present age of B?
questions.explanation_en: Let their ages six years ago be 6k and 5k. Four years hence: (6k + 10)/(5k + 10) = 11/10, so 60k + 100 = 55k + 110 and k = 2. Present ages: A = 18, B = 16.
questions.subtopic: Problems on ages – ratio of ages

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A and B start a business with capitals in the ratio 3/4 : 2/3. After 6 months, A withdraws one-third of his capital and B increases his capital by 50%. Out of a total profit of ₹1,40,000 at the end of the year, what is B's share?
questions.subtopic: Partnership – capital changed during the year

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: x varies directly as y² and inversely as z. When y = 4 and z = 8, x = 10. What is x when y = 6 and z = 12?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Percentage, Ratio, Average, Ages, Profit–Loss, SI–CI
questions.question_en: A loan of ₹21,000 is to be repaid in two equal annual instalments at 10% per annum compound interest. What is the amount of each instalment?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A and B together can do a job in 12 days. A alone can do it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.explanation_en: B's one-day work = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 1/30. So B alone takes 30 days.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. In how many days can 9 men complete the same work?
questions.explanation_en: Men × days is constant: 12 × 18 = 216. Days for 9 men = 216/9 = 24.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C in 12 days, and A and C in 24 days. In how many days can all three together do the work?

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they complete a work in 14 days. In how many days can B alone complete it?
questions.explanation_en: Let B's rate be b, so A's is 2b. 3b = 1/14, so b = 1/42. B alone takes 42 days.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They work together and are paid ₹3,000 in all. What is A's share?
questions.explanation_en: Shares are in the ratio of work done = 1/12 : 1/18 = 3 : 2. A gets 3/5 × 3000 = ₹1,800.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A can do a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They start together, but A leaves 5 days before the work is completed. In how many days is the whole work completed?
questions.explanation_en: Let the total time be x days. B works for x days and A for (x − 5) days: (x − 5)/20 + x/30 = 1. Multiply by 60: 3(x − 5) + 2x = 60, so 5x = 75 and x = 15.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours. A leak at the bottom can empty the full tank in 8 hours. If both are open, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation_en: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = (4 − 3)/24 = 1/24 per hour. So it takes 24 hours.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 10 and 15 minutes respectively, while pipe C can empty it in 30 minutes. If all three are opened together, in how much time will the empty tank be full?
questions.subtopic: Pipes & cisterns – inlet and outlet together

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A tank can be filled by a pipe in 4 hours and emptied by another pipe in 6 hours. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill half of the empty tank?
questions.explanation_en: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 per hour, so the full tank takes 12 hours. Half the tank takes 6 hours.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. Because of a leak, it takes 20 hours. How long will the leak take to empty the full tank?
questions.explanation_en: Leak rate = 1/15 − 1/20 = (4 − 3)/60 = 1/60. The leak empties the full tank in 60 hours.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 and 16 minutes respectively. Both are opened together, but A is closed after 4 minutes. How much more time will B need to fill the rest?
questions.explanation_en: In 4 minutes both fill 4 × (1/12 + 1/16) = 4 × 7/48 = 7/12 of the tank. Remaining 5/12 is filled by B at 1/16 per minute: (5/12) × 16 = 20/3 min = 6 min 40 sec.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Three pipes A, B and C can together fill a tank in 6 hours. After working together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B take 7 more hours to fill the rest. In how many hours can C alone fill the tank?
questions.explanation_en: In 2 hours, 2/6 = 1/3 is filled; 2/3 remains. A + B fill it in 7 hours, so A + B = (2/3)/7 = 2/21 per hour. C = 1/6 − 2/21 = (7 − 4)/42 = 1/14. So C alone takes 14 hours.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A man goes from his house to his office at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation_en: For equal distances the average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h. (The arithmetic mean 50 is the usual wrong answer.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Walking at 5/6 of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 12 minutes late. What is his usual time to reach the office?
questions.explanation_en: At 5/6 speed the time becomes 6/5 of the usual. So 6/5 T − T = T/5 = 12 min, giving T = 60 minutes.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Two persons start from the same point and walk in opposite directions at 5 km/h and 7 km/h. How far apart will they be after 3 hours?
questions.explanation_en: In opposite directions the speeds add: relative speed = 12 km/h. Distance = 12 × 3 = 36 km.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A cyclist covers 24 km at 12 km/h and then 36 km at 18 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation_en: Time for the first part = 24/12 = 2 h; second part = 36/18 = 2 h. Total distance = 60 km and total time = 4 h, so average speed = 15 km/h.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A policeman spots a thief 200 m away. The thief starts running at 10 km/h and the policeman chases him at 11 km/h. How far does the thief run before he is caught?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 1 km/h = 1000 m per hour. To close 200 m takes 0.2 hour. The thief runs 10 × 0.2 = 2 km = 2000 m (the policeman runs 2200 m).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Ramesh walks to school at 4 km/h and reaches 5 minutes late. At 5 km/h he reaches 10 minutes early. What is the distance to school?
questions.explanation_en: The difference in time = 15 min = 1/4 h. d/4 − d/5 = 1/4, so d/20 = 1/4 and d = 5 km.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A 180 m long train crosses a 270 m long platform in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation_en: Distance covered = 180 + 270 = 450 m in 30 s, so speed = 15 m/s = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Two trains of length 140 m and 160 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. In how many seconds will they cross each other?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s. Distance = 300 m. Time = 300 × 9/250 = 10.8 s.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Two trains of length 100 m and 150 m run in the same direction at 72 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. How long does the faster train take to completely overtake the slower one?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Distance to be covered = 100 + 150 = 250 m. Time = 250/5 = 50 s.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A 110 m long train passes a man walking in the opposite direction at 6 km/h in 6 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 110/6 m/s = 110/6 × 18/5 = 66 km/h. Since they move in opposite directions, train speed = 66 − 6 = 60 km/h.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A train running at 54 km/h takes 20 seconds to cross a platform and 12 seconds to pass a man standing on the platform. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation_en: Speed = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Train length = 15 × 12 = 180 m. Platform + train = 15 × 20 = 300 m, so platform = 120 m.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A train travelling at 48 km/h crosses another train, half its length and travelling in the opposite direction at 42 km/h, in 12 seconds. It also passes a platform in 45 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance in 12 s = 300 m = L + L/2, so L = 200 m. Train speed = 48 × 5/18 = 40/3 m/s; in 45 s it covers 600 m = L + platform, so platform = 600 − 200 = 400 m.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A boat covers 18 km downstream in 2 hours and 12 km upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream = 9 km/h, upstream = 6 km/h. Stream = (9 − 6)/2 = 1.5 km/h (still-water speed = 7.5 km/h).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How much time does it take to go 60 km downstream and come back?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream speed = 20 km/h, time = 3 h. Upstream speed = 10 km/h, time = 6 h. Total = 9 hours.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A man can row at 6 km/h in still water. In a river flowing at 2 km/h it takes him 3 hours to row to a place and come back. How far is the place?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream speed = 8 km/h, upstream = 4 km/h. d/8 + d/4 = 3 gives 3d/8 = 3, so d = 8 km.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A boat goes 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. It goes 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream in 13 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation_en: Let upstream speed u and downstream speed d. 30/u + 44/d = 10 and 40/u + 55/d = 13. Multiply the first by 4 and the second by 3: 120/u + 176/d = 40 and 120/u + 165/d = 39. Subtracting: 11/d = 1, so d = 11. Then 30/u = 10 − 4 = 6, so u = 5. Boat speed = (11 + 5)/2 = 8 km/h (stream = 3 km/h).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: In what ratio must rice at ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice at ₹55 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹46 per kg?
questions.explanation_en: By alligation, the ratio of cheaper : dearer = (55 − 46) : (46 − 40) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.explanation_en: Milk = 30 L, water = 10 L. For ratio 3 : 2 the water must be 30 × 2/3 = 20 L. Water to add = 20 − 10 = 10 L.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A vessel contains 60 litres of pure milk. 12 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. The process is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.explanation_en: Milk left = 60 × (1 − 12/60)² = 60 × (4/5)² = 60 × 16/25 = 38.4 litres. (48 L after the first step; 48 × 4/5 = 38.4 after the second.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: Two vessels contain milk and water in the ratios 2 : 3 and 3 : 4. If equal quantities of the two mixtures are poured into a third vessel, what is the ratio of milk to water in it?
questions.explanation_en: Take 35 units from each vessel. Vessel 1: milk 14, water 21. Vessel 2: milk 15, water 20. Total milk = 29, water = 41. Ratio = 29 : 41.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A milkman mixes water with milk and sells the mixture at the cost price of pure milk. If his gain is 20%, what is the ratio of water to milk in the mixture?
questions.explanation_en: For every 5 litres of milk bought (cost 5), he sells 6 litres of mixture (revenue 6), a gain of 1/5 = 20%. So 1 litre of water is added to 5 litres of milk: water : milk = 1 : 5.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Time & Work, Pipes, Speed–Distance, Trains, Boats, Mixtures
questions.question_en: A bus covers the first one-third of a journey at 30 km/h, the next one-third at 40 km/h and the last one-third at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation_en: Take the journey as 120 km (40 km per part). Time = 40/30 + 40/40 + 40/60 = 4/3 + 1 + 2/3 = 3 h. Average speed = 120/3 = 40 km/h. 43 1/3 is the simple mean of the speeds, which is wrong for equal distances.
questions.subtopic: Speed – average speed over three equal distances

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If x + 1/x = 5, then the value of x² + 1/x² is:
questions.explanation_en: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23. The trap answer 27 adds 2 instead of subtracting it.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If a + b + c = 0 and abc = 4, then a³ + b³ + c³ is:
questions.explanation_en: Identity: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). With a + b + c = 0, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc = 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The roots of the quadratic equation 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0 are:
questions.explanation_en: Split the middle term: 2x² − 6x − x + 3 = 2x(x − 3) − 1(x − 3) = (2x − 1)(x − 3). So x = 3 or x = 1/2. Check: sum 7/2 = −b/a and product 3/2 = c/a.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0, then α² + β² equals:
questions.explanation_en: α + β = 5 and αβ = 6. α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 25 − 12 = 13. (Roots are 2 and 3: 4 + 9 = 13.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: For what values of k does the equation x² + kx + 16 = 0 have two equal real roots?
questions.explanation_en: Equal roots need discriminant b² − 4ac = 0: k² − 64 = 0, so k = ±8. Taking only the positive root (8) misses k = −8.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If 2x + 3y = 13 and 3x − y = 3, then x + y equals:
questions.explanation_en: From the second equation y = 3x − 3. Substituting: 2x + 9x − 9 = 13 → 11x = 22 → x = 2, y = 3. So x + y = 5.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If a − b = 3 and a³ − b³ = 117, then the value of ab is:
questions.explanation_en: a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b). So 117 = 27 + 9ab → 9ab = 90 → ab = 10. (Check: a = 5, b = 2.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The value of sin 30° + cos 60° is:
questions.explanation_en: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so the sum is 1.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is acute, then sin θ is:
questions.explanation_en: Take opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, so hypotenuse = √(9 + 16) = 5. sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The value of (1 − sin²θ) × sec²θ is:
questions.explanation_en: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, and cos²θ × sec²θ = cos²θ × 1/cos²θ = 1.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The value of tan 10° × tan 20° × tan 70° × tan 80° is:
questions.explanation_en: tan 80° = cot 10° and tan 70° = cot 20°. So the product = (tan 10° cot 10°)(tan 20° cot 20°) = 1 × 1 = 1.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If sin 3θ = cos(θ − 6°), where 3θ and (θ − 6°) are acute angles, then θ equals:
questions.explanation_en: sin A = cos B with both acute means A + B = 90°. So 3θ + θ − 6° = 90° → 4θ = 96° → θ = 24°.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: From a point on the ground 30 m away from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. The height of the tower is:
questions.explanation_en: tan 60° = height / 30 → height = 30 × √3 = 30√3 m (≈ 51.96 m). 10√3 m would result from using tan 30° by mistake.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The shadow of a tower becomes 40 m shorter when the Sun's altitude increases from 30° to 60°. The height of the tower is:

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If sec θ + tan θ = 4, then sec θ − tan θ equals:
questions.explanation_en: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, i.e. (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1. So sec θ − tan θ = 1/4.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If sec θ + tan θ = 4, then sin θ equals:
questions.explanation_en: sec θ − tan θ = 1/4 (since sec²θ − tan²θ = 1). Adding: 2 sec θ = 17/4 → sec θ = 17/8; subtracting: tan θ = 15/8. sin θ = tan θ / sec θ = 15/17.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The value of cos 0° + sin 90° + tan 45° is:
questions.explanation_en: cos 0° = 1, sin 90° = 1 and tan 45° = 1, so the sum is 3.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: A ladder 20 m long leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation_en: Height = ladder × sin 60° = 20 × √3/2 = 10√3 m (≈ 17.32 m). 10 m is the distance of the foot from the wall (20 cos 60°).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: What is the remainder when x³ − 2x² + 4x − 5 is divided by (x − 2)?
questions.explanation_en: By the remainder theorem, put x = 2: 8 − 8 + 8 − 5 = 3.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: If sin θ + cos θ = √2, then the value of sin θ cos θ is:
questions.explanation_en: Square both sides: sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ = 2, i.e. 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 2, so sin θ cos θ = 1/2 (θ = 45°).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: The value of sin²25° + sin²65° + tan 30° × tan 60° is:
questions.explanation_en: sin 65° = cos 25°, so sin²25° + sin²65° = sin²25° + cos²25° = 1. tan 30° × tan 60° = (1/√3) × √3 = 1. Total = 2.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Algebra & Trigonometry Basics
questions.question_en: From the top of a building 60 m high, the angle of depression of a car on the road is 30°. How far is the car from the foot of the building?
questions.explanation_en: Angle of depression = angle of elevation from the car = 30°. tan 30° = 60/d, so d = 60/(1/√3) = 60√3 m (≈ 103.9 m). 20√3 m comes from wrongly using tan 60°.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is:
questions.explanation_en: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180° = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. The number of sides of the polygon is:
questions.explanation_en: Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°, so n = 360 / 24 = 15.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. The largest angle is:

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one of the two interior opposite angles is 45°. The other interior opposite angle is:
questions.explanation_en: Exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles, so the other angle = 110° − 45° = 65°.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: In a circle of radius 13 cm, a chord is 24 cm long. The distance of the chord from the centre is:
questions.explanation_en: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: half-chord = 12 cm. Distance = √(13² − 12²) = √25 = 5 cm.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: A point P is 25 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 7 cm. The length of the tangent drawn from P to the circle is:
questions.explanation_en: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so tangent = √(25² − 7²) = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at a point P inside the circle. If AP = 6 cm, PB = 4 cm and CP = 3 cm, then PD is:
questions.explanation_en: By the intersecting chords theorem, AP × PB = CP × PD → 6 × 4 = 3 × PD → PD = 8 cm.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 120° at the centre. The angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part (major arc) of the circle is:
questions.explanation_en: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle: 120° / 2 = 60°.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which ∠A = 70° and ∠B = 95°. The measure of ∠C is:
questions.explanation_en: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: ∠C = 180° − ∠A = 180° − 70° = 110°. (∠D = 180° − 95° = 85°, the trap answer.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: In a triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, the length of the median drawn to the longest side is:
questions.explanation_en: 6² + 8² = 100 = 10², so the triangle is right-angled with hypotenuse 10 cm. The median to the hypotenuse equals half of it (the midpoint is the circumcentre): 5 cm.
questions.subtopic: Geometry – median of a right triangle

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 16 : 25. The ratio of their corresponding altitudes is:
questions.explanation_en: For similar triangles, ratio of areas = square of the ratio of corresponding sides, altitudes or medians. So altitude ratio = √16 : √25 = 4 : 5.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: In triangle ABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 2 cm and AE = 4.5 cm, then EC is:
questions.explanation_en: By the Basic Proportionality (Thales) theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC → 3/2 = 4.5/EC → EC = 3 cm.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. The perimeter of the rhombus is:
questions.explanation_en: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so side = √(8² + 6²) = 10 cm and perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40 cm. 96 cm² is its area (½ × 16 × 12).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The volume of a cube is 343 cm³. Its total surface area is:
questions.explanation_en: Side = ∛343 = 7 cm. Total surface area = 6a² = 6 × 49 = 294 cm². 196 cm² is the lateral surface area (4a²).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The volume of a right circular cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is (take π = 22/7):
questions.explanation_en: V = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 10 = 154 × 10 = 1540 cm³. 440 cm² is the curved surface area 2πrh, a common mix-up.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The curved surface area of a right circular cone of base radius 6 cm and height 8 cm is:
questions.explanation_en: Slant height l = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm. Curved surface area = πrl = π × 6 × 10 = 60π cm². Using the height instead of the slant height gives the wrong 48π.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small solid cones, each of base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. How many cones are formed?
questions.explanation_en: Sphere volume = (4/3)π × 216 = 288π. Cone volume = (1/3)π × 9 × 4 = 12π. Number of cones = 288π / 12π = 24.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 21 cm is (take π = 22/7):
questions.explanation_en: TSA of a solid hemisphere = curved 2πr² + flat base πr² = 3πr² = 3 × 22/7 × 441 = 4158 cm². 2772 cm² is only the curved part.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: A rectangular park is 60 m long and 40 m wide. A path 5 m wide runs all around it on the outside. The area of the path is:
questions.explanation_en: Outer rectangle = (60 + 10) × (40 + 10) = 70 × 50 = 3500 m². Park = 60 × 40 = 2400 m². Path = 3500 − 2400 = 1100 m². Adding only 5 m (not 2 × 5) to each side is the usual error.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: If the radius of a circle is increased by 10%, its area increases by:
questions.explanation_en: Area ∝ r². New area factor = 1.1² = 1.21, an increase of 21%. Equivalently a + b + ab/100 = 10 + 10 + 1 = 21%.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: A cuboid of dimensions 12 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm is melted and recast into cubes of side 2 cm. How many cubes are obtained?
questions.explanation_en: Cuboid volume = 12 × 8 × 6 = 576 cm³. Each cube = 2³ = 8 cm³. Number of cubes = 576 / 8 = 72.

questions.question_en: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm is:

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: What is the area of the circle that circumscribes a triangle with sides 20 cm, 21 cm and 29 cm?
questions.explanation_en: 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841 = 29², so the triangle is right-angled and the hypotenuse is the diameter of the circumcircle. R = 29/2 = 14.5 cm; area = π × 14.5² = 210.25π cm². 841π uses the hypotenuse as the radius.
questions.subtopic: Geometry – circumcircle of a right triangle

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: The area of the ring between two concentric circles is 286 cm² and the difference of their radii is 7 cm. What is the radius of the outer circle? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation_en: π(R² − r²) = 286, so R² − r² = 286 × 7/22 = 91. Since (R − r)(R + r) = 91 and R − r = 7, R + r = 13. Adding: 2R = 20, so R = 10 cm (r = 3 cm).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: Two solid cones, each of base radius 6 cm and heights 10 cm and 14 cm, are melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the surface area of the sphere?
questions.explanation_en: Total volume = (1/3)π × 6² × (10 + 14) = (1/3)π × 36 × 24 = 288π. (4/3)πR³ = 288π gives R³ = 216, so R = 6 cm. Surface area = 4πR² = 4π × 36 = 144π cm². 288π is the volume, not the area.
questions.subtopic: Mensuration – cones recast into a sphere

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: A right circular cylinder of height 10 cm is inscribed in a sphere of radius 13 cm. What is the volume of the cylinder?
questions.explanation_en: The centre of the sphere is at mid-height, 5 cm from each base. Cylinder radius r = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm. Volume = πr²h = π × 144 × 10 = 1440π cm³.
questions.subtopic: Mensuration – cylinder inscribed in a sphere

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: If each edge of a cube is increased by 20%, by what percentage does its total surface area increase?
questions.explanation_en: Surface area ∝ edge². New factor = 1.2² = 1.44, an increase of 44% (shortcut 20 + 20 + 20 × 20/100 = 44). 72.8% is the increase in volume (1.2³ = 1.728).
questions.subtopic: Mensuration – percentage change in surface area

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: A cylinder of base radius 4 cm and height 9 cm has the same volume as a cone of height 12 cm. What is the curved surface area of the cone?
questions.explanation_en: Cylinder volume = π × 16 × 9 = 144π. (1/3)πr² × 12 = 144π gives r² = 36, so r = 6 cm. Slant height l = √(6² + 12²) = √180 = 6√5 cm. Curved surface = πrl = π × 6 × 6√5 = 36√5π cm².
questions.subtopic: Mensuration – cylinder and cone of equal volume

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Geometry & Mensuration
questions.question_en: What is the radius of the circle inscribed in a triangle with sides 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm?
questions.explanation_en: 8² + 15² = 289 = 17², a right triangle. Inradius r = Area/s = (½ × 8 × 15)/20 = 60/20 = 3 cm. Shortcut for a right triangle: r = (a + b − c)/2 = (8 + 15 − 17)/2 = 3 cm.
questions.subtopic: Geometry – inradius of a right triangle

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
Which school has the highest pass percentage?
questions.explanation_en: Pass % = passed/appeared × 100: P 75%, Q 85%, R 65%, S 80%, T 90%. T is highest; S has the most passes but not the highest rate.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
What is the overall pass percentage of all five schools taken together (approximately)?
questions.explanation_en: Total appeared = 240 + 300 + 180 + 360 + 220 = 1300; total passed = 180 + 255 + 117 + 288 + 198 = 1038. 1038/1300 × 100 ≈ 79.85%. Averaging the five percentages (79%) is wrong because school sizes differ.

questions.explanation_en: Total passed = 1038. Average = 1038 / 5 = 207.6. 260 is the average number appeared (1300/5).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
The number of students who failed in school S is what percent of the number who failed in school R (approximately)?
questions.explanation_en: Failed in S = 360 − 288 = 72; failed in R = 180 − 117 = 63. 72/63 × 100 ≈ 114.29%. Inverting the ratio gives 87.5%.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288

In how many schools is the pass percentage higher than the overall pass percentage of all five schools combined?
questions.explanation_en: Overall = 1038/1300 ≈ 79.85%. School pass %: P 75, Q 85, R 65, S 80, T 90. Q, S and T exceed 79.85%, so the answer is 3 (S just qualifies at 80%).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
By what percent did laptop production increase from 2020 to 2023?
questions.explanation_en: Increase = 60 − 40 = 20 thousand. Percent increase = 20/40 × 100 = 50%. 33.3% wrongly divides by the final value (20/60).

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The arithmetic mean of the first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.explanation_en: Sum = 10 × 11 / 2 = 55, so the mean = 55 / 10 = 5.5. In general the mean of the first n natural numbers is (n + 1)/2.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The median of the data 7, 3, 9, 4, 12, 6 is:
questions.explanation_en: Arrange in order: 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12. With an even count (6), median = average of the 3rd and 4th values = (6 + 7)/2 = 6.5. 6.83 is the mean, not the median.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The mode of the data 2, 3, 5, 3, 7, 5, 3, 8 is:
questions.explanation_en: 3 occurs three times, more than any other value (5 occurs twice), so the mode is 3.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: For a moderately skewed distribution, the mean is 25 and the median is 24. Using the empirical relation, the mode is:
questions.explanation_en: Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean = 3 × 24 − 2 × 25 = 72 − 50 = 22.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The mean of five numbers is 20. When one number is removed, the mean of the remaining four numbers becomes 18. The number removed is:
questions.explanation_en: Sum of five = 5 × 20 = 100; sum of four = 4 × 18 = 72. Removed number = 100 − 72 = 28.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The average marks of 30 students was found to be 60. Later it was found that one student's marks were read as 75 instead of 45. The correct average is:
questions.explanation_en: Wrong total = 30 × 60 = 1800. Correct total = 1800 − 75 + 45 = 1770. Correct average = 1770 / 30 = 59.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: Find the mean of the following frequency distribution. Values (x): 10, 20, 30, 40. Frequencies (f): 3, 5, 8, 4.
questions.explanation_en: Σfx = 10×3 + 20×5 + 30×8 + 40×4 = 30 + 100 + 240 + 160 = 530. Σf = 20. Mean = 530 / 20 = 26.5. The simple average of the values (25) ignores the frequencies.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The range of the data 15, 22, 8, 31, 19 is:
questions.explanation_en: Range = largest − smallest = 31 − 8 = 23.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is:
questions.explanation_en: Mean = 30 / 5 = 6. Squared deviations: 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 → sum 40. Variance = 40 / 5 = 8, so SD = √8 = 2√2 ≈ 2.83. 8 is the variance, not the SD.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The percentage profit of companies X and Y in four years is given below (in text form).
Year | X | Y
2019 | 20% | 30%
2020 | 25% | 40%
2021 | 40% | 35%
2022 | 30% | 50%
Percentage profit = (Income − Expenditure)/Expenditure × 100.
If the expenditure of company X in 2020 was ₹240 crore, what was its income in that year?
questions.explanation_en: Income = Expenditure × (1 + profit%/100) = 240 × 1.25 = ₹300 crore. ₹288 crore wrongly uses X's 2019 profit of 20%.
questions.subtopic: Data interpretation – percentage profit (income and expenditure)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The percentage profit of companies X and Y in four years is given below (in text form).
Year | X | Y
2019 | 20% | 30%
2020 | 25% | 40%
2021 | 40% | 35%
2022 | 30% | 50%
Percentage profit = (Income − Expenditure)/Expenditure × 100.
If the income of company Y in 2021 was ₹270 crore, what was its expenditure in that year?
questions.explanation_en: Income = 1.35 × Expenditure, so Expenditure = 270/1.35 = ₹200 crore. ₹175.5 crore wrongly takes 35% off the income (270 × 0.65).
questions.subtopic: Data interpretation – percentage profit (income and expenditure)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics

In 2022 the expenditures of X and Y were equal, and their total income was ₹504 crore. What was the expenditure of each company?
questions.explanation_en: Let each expenditure be E. Income of X = 1.3E and of Y = 1.5E, so 2.8E = 504 and E = ₹180 crore.
questions.subtopic: Data interpretation – percentage profit (income and expenditure)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en:
The percentage profit of companies X and Y in four years is given below (in text form).
Year | X | Y
2019 | 20% | 30%
2020 | 25% | 40%
2021 | 40% | 35%
2022 | 30% | 50%
Percentage profit = (Income − Expenditure)/Expenditure × 100.
If the incomes of X and Y were equal in 2019, what was the ratio of the expenditure of X to that of Y?
questions.explanation_en: Expenditure = Income/(1 + profit%). With equal income I: X = I/1.2 and Y = I/1.3. Ratio = 1/1.2 : 1/1.3 = 1.3 : 1.2 = 13 : 12.
questions.subtopic: Data interpretation – percentage profit (income and expenditure)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The mean marks of 30 boys in a class are 60 and the mean marks of 20 girls are 70. What are the mean marks of the whole class?
questions.explanation_en: Combined mean = (30 × 60 + 20 × 70)/(30 + 20) = (1800 + 1400)/50 = 3200/50 = 64. The simple average of 60 and 70 (65) ignores the group sizes.

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: What is the median of 21, 15, 34, 18, 27, 40 and 12?
questions.explanation_en: Arrange in order: 12, 15, 18, 21, 27, 34, 40. With 7 values the median is the 4th value, 21. (The mean is 167/7 ≈ 23.9.)

questions.chapter: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability — Data Interpretation & Statistics
questions.question_en: The mean of 10 observations is 25. If 5 is added to each observation and every result is then multiplied by 2, what is the new mean?
questions.explanation_en: The mean follows the same operations as each value: (25 + 5) × 2 = 60. 55 comes from doing the steps in the wrong order (25 × 2 + 5).
questions.subtopic: Statistics – effect of changing every observation
